evidence.claim: The cached Serenity methodology requires starting from a broad theme, breaking it into demand drivers, supply-chain nodes, bottlenecks, public-market mappings, evidence, market-pricing checks, and falsification plans.

The cached Serenity methodology prioritizes layers with low supplier count, long validation cycles, strict customer certification, material constraints, expansion difficulty, and substitution difficulty; this lowers the initial bottleneck score for generic software unless customer/revenue evidence proves a hard-to-replace control point.

Cloudflare reported Q1 2026 revenue of $639.8 million, up 34% year over year, with dollar-based net retention of 118%, 4,416 customers paying more than $100,000 per year, and free cash flow of $84.1 million.
evidence.source_title: Cloudflare NET Q1 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

evidence.claim: Cloudflare's reported growth, large-customer expansion, and developer-platform activity support a plausible second-order AI/cloud relationship, but the evidence does not yet prove that AI inference or agent workloads are a distinct revenue chokepoint rather than part of broader security and connectivity growth.
evidence.source_title: Cloudflare Announces First Quarter 2026 Financial Results

evidence.claim: Datadog reported Q1 2026 revenue growth of 32% year over year to $1.006 billion and disclosed product activity including MCP Server availability for AI coding agents and secure, real-time access to unified observability data.
evidence.source_title: Datadog Announces First Quarter 2026 Financial Results

evidence.claim: Datadog announced more than 100 new capabilities at DASH 2026 focused on autonomy, AI, security complexity, development workflows, security workflows, and operational workflows.
evidence.source_title: Datadog Launches 100+ Capabilities to Help Customers Drive Autonomy and Manage Growing AI and Security Complexity

evidence.claim: Datadog has the strongest direct software-node fit in this chunk because AI and cloud complexity plausibly increase observability, security analytics, and operations automation demand; however, Layer 2B still requires customer and usage evidence showing incremental AI workload monetization.
SentinelOne reported Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue growth of 20% year over year, ARR growth of 22% to $1.1191 billion, 1,667 customers with ARR of $100,000 or more, and non-GAAP operating margin of 6%.
evidence.source_title: SentinelOne Announces Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results

evidence.claim: SentinelOne management stated that customers are standardizing on Singularity for securing AI and autonomous cybersecurity and said the company secures pioneers building frontier AI models, while also reporting full-year fiscal 2026 revenue of $1.0013 billion, up 22%.
evidence.source_title: SentinelOne Announces Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results

evidence.claim: SentinelOne may be a smaller, underfollowed AI-security beneficiary, but current evidence is not sufficient to prove AI workloads are causing durable incremental ARR growth rather than general cybersecurity platform adoption.
evidence.source_title: SentinelOne Announces Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results

evidence.source_title: IBM Completes Acquisition of HashiCorp, Creates Comprehensive, End-to-End Hybrid Cloud Platform

evidence.claim: HashiCorp's infrastructure automation exposure should be remapped to IBM only as a diluted reference relationship because IBM's broader hybrid-cloud, consulting, mainframe, AI, and software portfolio reduces the purity of the original HCP thesis.
evidence.source_title: IBM Completes Acquisition of HashiCorp, Creates Comprehensive, End-to-End Hybrid Cloud Platform

memory_update.text: NET mapped to second-order AI/cloud software via edge networking, application security, connectivity, and developer platform; retain as hypothesis pending proof of AI inference/developer workload monetization, DBNR durability, and capex efficiency.

DDOG mapped to observability, AI operations, cloud complexity, and security software; strongest direct software relationship in this chunk, but still requires AI-specific usage and net retention evidence before being treated as a durable chokepoint.
S mapped to AI-enabled endpoint/cloud/security automation as an underfollowed mid-cap hypothesis; evidence supports ARR growth and AI-security positioning but not yet causal AI-driven growth.
HCP should be removed from the standalone public-company universe because IBM completed the HashiCorp acquisition on 2025-02-27.
IBM may be used only as a reference mapping for HashiCorp infrastructure automation exposure; do not treat it as an underfollowed pure-play candidate.

Software lane requires stronger Layer 2C evidence: AI-specific revenue contribution, cohort expansion, DBNR or NRR trends, customer case studies, gross margin/capex sensitivity, pricing power, and competitive displacement versus hyperscaler-native tools or open-source alternatives.

Market-pricing checks are still missing for NET, DDOG, S, and IBM: refresh current market cap, EV/revenue, revenue-growth expectations, analyst coverage, short interest, ownership quality, and whether AI exposure is already fully priced.

summary: Mapped the candidate chunk as a second-order AI/cloud software lane rather than a primary physical chokepoint. Cloudflare, Datadog, and SentinelOne have direct public-market relationships to cloud complexity, AI deployment, security automation, developer infrastructure, or observability, but the Serenity bottleneck claim remains weaker than for hardware, power, substrates, packaging, test, or grid nodes because software exposure must be proven through revenue acceleration, net retention, customer expansion, and durable margin leverage. HashiCorp should be removed as a standalone ticker relationship because IBM completed its acquisition in February 2025; any continuing HashiCorp exposure is now embedded inside IBM and is too diluted for an underfollowed small/mid-cap candidate lane.

This is one of the cleaner software mappings in the chunk, but still needs proof that AI-related usage is incremental rather than bundled into general cloud growth.

The relationship is that expansion of AI workloads, AI-native enterprises, and autonomous security operations may increase demand for automated threat detection and response. Compared with Cloudflare and Datadog, SentinelOne is more underfollowed and smaller, but the evidence must distinguish AI-security revenue pull from broad cybersecurity platform growth.
